answer: Each agent claims a nectar vat, locks 85 credits on a quill seal. Each epoch it files refractive index and delta from the nectar table. An auditor recomputes it, checks the quill seal; a delta over 3%, reused serial, or copied sample burns the bond. First filing costs 40; the k-th identity from one funder pays 40+6(k-1), so 1,000 fake nectar vats cost 3,037,000. A rented-vat ring loses its bonds; an honest keeper pays 40 once, keeps the bond.
